results.title: From GPUs to RRAMs: Distributed In-Memory Primal–Dual Hybrid Gradient Method for Solving Large-Scale Linear Optimization Problems
results.content: These results demonstrate the first PDHG-based LP solver implemented on RRAMs, showcasing the transformative potential of algorithm–hardware co-design for solving large-scale optimization through distributed in-memory computing. Interestingly, the developers of commercial LP solvers have also begun integrating PDHG: Gurobi reports that an experimental PDHG algorithm can be competitive with its highly optimized simplex and interior-point methods on certain large-scale LPs. These studies underscore that a matrix–vector-centric iterative solver can scale to problem sizes beyond the reach of factorization-based solvers, especially when paired with parallel architectures. We provide theoretical convergence bounds for PDHG under analog noise in RRAM-based implementations, which guarantee that in-memory PDHG remains convergent on noisy RRAM hardware under mild conditions, and the rate is provably no worse than conventional computing implementation up to a fixed error term. ‣ 4.2 Inexact In-Memory PDHG Updates ‣ 4 Theoretical Guarantees ‣ From GPUs to RRAMs: Distributed In-Memory Primal–Dual Hybrid Gradient Method for Solving Large-Scale Linear Optimization Problems") provides a rule for safely choosing step sizes for the PDHG algorithm when the operator norm, , is estimated with some error. ‣ 4.2 Inexact In-Memory PDHG Updates ‣ 4 Theoretical Guarantees ‣ From GPUs to RRAMs: Distributed In-Memory Primal–Dual Hybrid Gradient Method for Solving Large-Scale Linear Optimization Problems") presents a one-step inequality that describes the progress of the PDHG algorithm in the presence of noise. ‣ 4.2 Inexact In-Memory PDHG Updates ‣ 4 Theoretical Guarantees ‣ From GPUs to RRAMs: Distributed In-Memory Primal–Dual Hybrid Gradient Method for Solving Large-Scale Linear Optimization Problems") establishes the convergence rate for the PDHG algorithm when operating under the defined noise assumptions. By employing the more robust Lanczos iteration for operator norm estimation and providing theoretical guarantees for the convergence of PDHG under noisy updates, we establish that RRAM-based IMC is a viable and reliable platform for high-precision iterative algorithms. In this paper, we establish the significant potential of RRAM-based in-memory computing for solving linear optimization problems through iterative PDHG. ‣ 4.2 Inexact In-Memory PDHG Updates ‣ 4 Theoretical Guarantees ‣ From GPUs to RRAMs: Distributed In-Memory Primal–Dual Hybrid Gradient Method for Solving Large-Scale Linear Optimization Problems").

We introduce the decentralized Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno (D-BFGS) method as a variation of the BFGS quasi-Newton method for solving decentralized optimization problems. We introduce the distributed Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (D-BFGS) method as an asynchronous decentralized variation of the BFGS quasi-Newton method for solving consensus optimization problems on…. ### A decentralized quasi-Newton method for dual formulations of consensus optimization. This work proposes a line search free greedy quasi-Newton method with adaptive steps and establishes explicit non-asymptotic bounds for both the global convergence rate and local superlinear rate and proposes a distributed adaptive GQN method whose communication cost is comparable with that of first-order methods, yet it retains the superb convergence property of its centralized counterpart. ### A Primal-Dual Quasi-Newton Method for Exact Consensus Optimization. This work derives fully decentralized quasi-Newton updates that approximate second order information to reduce the computational burden relative to dual methods and to make the method more robust in ill-conditioned problems relative to first order methods. ### A primal-dual Quasi-Newton method for consensus optimization. The PD-QN method performs quasi-Newton, or approximate second order, updates on both the primal and dual variables of the consensus optimization problem to remove the internal minimization step necessary in most dual methods and also make the method more robust in ill-conditioned settings relative to first order methods. We introduce the distributed Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (D-BFGS) method as an asynchronous decentralized variation of the BFGS quasi-Newton method for solving consensus optimization problems on…. ### A decentralized quasi-Newton method for dual formulations of consensus optimization. ### A Decentralized Second-Order Method with Exact Linear Convergence Rate for Consensus Optimization. This paper proposes the network Newton (NN) method as a distributed algorithm that incorporates second-order information via distributed implementation of approximations of a suitably chosen Newton step and proves convergence to a point close to the optimal argument at a rate that is at least linear. This work uses a family of dual descent algorithms that approximate the Newton direction to achieve faster convergence rates than existing distributed methods to solve the convex network flow optimization problem.
